column3: The Hebrew names each of the seven peoples with a singular collective noun; BSB uses plural names.
The Hebrew separately states that you will strike them and uses “cut a covenant”; BSB gives “to defeat them” and “Make no treaty.”
The Hebrew uses singular “your daughter,” “his son,” “his daughter,” and “your son”; BSB uses plural daughters and sons throughout.
The Hebrew begins with singular “he will turn your son” and then changes to plural “they will serve”; BSB begins with plural “they” and “your sons.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “all the peoples” in both comparisons; BSB first says “the other peoples” and then “all peoples.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew joins “the covenant” and “the loving devotion” with “and”; BSB combines them as “His covenant of loving devotion.”
The Hebrew initially refers to the haters in the plural but to the recipient’s face and destruction in the singular; BSB initially uses plural “their faces.”
The Hebrew has singular “the commandment”; BSB has plural “the commandments.”
The Hebrew separately says to listen, keep, and do the ordinances; BSB says to listen and “keep them carefully.”
The Hebrew repeats “fruit” for the womb and the ground; BSB uses “fruit” and then “produce.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls these “the evil diseases of Egypt”; BSB expresses this as diseases “you knew in Egypt.”
The Hebrew says to “eat” the peoples and that your “eye” must not pity them; BSB says “destroy” and “Do not look on them with pity.”
The Hebrew uses singular “me” and “I” in the quoted question; BSB uses plural “we.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “your eyes saw”; BSB says “you saw.”
The Hebrew joins “the remaining” and “the hidden” with “and”; BSB combines them as “the survivors hiding from you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “you cannot” and uses singular collective “the beast of the field”; BSB says “will not be enabled” and uses plural “wild animals.”
The Hebrew repeats the confusion root in a verb and noun; BSB expresses this as “throw them into great confusion.”

The Hebrew has singular “their name” and explicitly names “your hand”; BSB has plural “their names” and uses the verb “hand ... over.” The Hebrew links the final destruction with “until,” while BSB gives it as a separate statement.
The Hebrew explicitly says “in the fire” and uses singular “for yourself”; BSB says “burn up” and plural “for yourselves.”
Close to the Hebrew.
